newsitem.title: USA: Hilton says $55/shr ITT bid is solid.
newsitem.headline: Hilton says $55/shr ITT bid is solid.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp will continue to pursue what it believes is a solid $55 per share bid for ITT Corp despite ITT's rejection of the offer earlier on Wednesday, a Hilton spokesman said.
"In a nutshell, nothing in their response changes our plans or our intent," Marc Grossman, senior vice president corporate affairs, told Reuters. "We put a strong offer on the table."
He said ITT's plan for a legal challenge to Hilton's offer and ITT's allegations of misappropriation and misuse of confidential information are "without merit."
Late last month, Hilton launched a $6.5 billion cash and stock offer for shares ITT with the goal of acquiring ITT's chain of Sheraton hotels and Caesars World Inc casinos.
Hilton said it would likely sell assets such as ITT's Madison Square Garden and ITT Educational Services.
Earlier Wednesday, ITT roundly rejected the bid, labeling it inadequate and not in the best interest of shareholders.
ITT also said it would seek a sale of the non-core assets.

In a stern letter to ITT Chairman Rand Araskog, delivered on Tuesday, Hilton Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach warned ITT that if it sold assets to make ITT less attractive, Hilton might simply lower its offer.
"If you just take the language that's in the letter and that tone, nothing happened today to move us off that position," Grossman said.
Grossman also reiterated Hilton's position that if it could meet with ITT management and review the company's financial situation, it might be persuaded to change its offer.
Until now, Hilton has used publicly available information to calculate its offer, it has said.
Absent any contact with ITT management, its $55 per share bid currently remains unchanged, Grossman said.
